title: Waimoa language - Wikipedia
text: Waimoa or Waimaʼa is a language spoken by about 27,000 Waimoa people in northeast East Timor. Waimoa proper is reported to be mutually intelligible with neighboring Kairui and Midiki, which together have about 5,000 speakers.

title: Waima’a | Ethnologue Free
text: Waima’a is an endangered indigenous language of East Timor. It belongs to the Austronesian language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by a decreasing number of young people.

title: The sounds of Waima'a - DOBES
text: The sounds of Waima’a. Waima’a has a very complex phonological inventory compared with other languages from East Timor, or indeed compared with most Austronesian languages anywhere else.
